title: Your First C Program
instructions: Welcome! Every journey into C starts the same way: making the computer say something back to you.
Look at the code. A few pieces do the work:
- #include <stdio.h> loads C's input/output toolbox. That's where printf lives — the tool for printing text.
- int main() { ... } is the starting line of every C program. When you run it, the computer finds main and runs whatever is inside its curly braces { }.
- printf("...") prints whatever text is between the quotes.
- Every statement ends with a semicolon ;  Forgetting it is the #1 beginner mistake.
- return 0; means 'all done, everything went fine.'
task: Make the program print exactly:  Hello, World!
